title: Observability (logging, metrics, distributed tracing, alerting, SLO/SLA)
relevance: High — almost every HLD ends with "how do you know it's healthy / on fire?"; interviewers probe golden signals, p99 vs avg, structured logs + trace IDs, and SLI/SLO/SLA vs error budget. Full "design Datadog/Prometheus" is common in mid/senior loops.
company_notes: Near-universal closing reliability discussion on any HLD. Campus/new-grad: light—monitoring, latency/errors/QPS, maybe centralized logs; SLO vocabulary is a plus. Mid (1–4 YOE): SLO/error budget, p99, cardinality, microservice tracing, design-metrics-platform common at Meta, Google, Uber, Amazon, Stripe, Atlassian, Flipkart. Standalone design Datadog/CloudWatch/Prometheus is a frequent senior/infra question; depth is tradeoffs and incident workflow, not building a TSDB.

phases.goal: Establish observability vs monitoring, the three pillars, golden signals, and why percentiles beat averages.

must_hit.point: Monitoring asks known questions from alerts/dashboards; observability lets you ask new questions from correlated logs, metrics, and traces.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts 'is error rate above a threshold?' with 'why is this checkout slow for this user?' via linked telemetry.

must_hit.point: Three pillars: logs are discrete high-context events; metrics are aggregatable time series cheap to store/alert; traces are one request as a tree of spans.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names logs/metrics/traces and default interview stack: structured logs + Prometheus-style metrics + OTel/Jaeger, linked by trace_id.

must_hit.point: Four golden signals for user-facing systems: latency (success vs failure), traffic, errors (explicit + wrong answers), saturation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists latency, traffic, errors, saturation and notes separating success vs failure latency.

must_hit.point: Prefer p50/p95/p99 over average latency because averages hide the tail.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says avg hides outliers and that p99 vs SLO is a common alert/interview answer.

probes: What is the difference between monitoring and observability, and what are the three pillars?
Name the four golden signals and say why you track percentiles instead of average latency.

hints.1: Think about what you can ask after an alert fires versus only knowing if a known threshold breached.
hints.2: Logs = events, metrics = numbers over time, traces = request path as spans; golden signals are latency/traffic/errors/saturation.
hints.3: Observability = new questions from correlated telemetry; track p50/p95/p99 because averages hide the tail.

phases.goal: Explain SLI/SLO/SLA, error budgets, structured logs, tracing propagation/sampling, cardinality, and symptom-based alerting.

must_hit.point: SLI is the measured indicator; SLO is the internal target over a window; SLA is the customer contract and is usually looser than the SLO.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks indicator → internal target → contractual promise and says never set SLA equal to SLO with no buffer.

must_hit.point: Error budget is 1 − SLO (e.g. 99.9% → 0.1% bad events / ~43 min downtime per month); spent budget throttles releases toward reliability work.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines budget as remaining unreliability, ties it to change velocity, and mentions freeze/reliability work when exhausted.

must_hit.point: Structured logs (JSON-like) carry level, service, timestamp, request_id/trace_id and business ids so you can search and jump pillars.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects printf spaghetti; names fields that make ELK/Loki correlation possible.

must_hit.point: Distributed tracing propagates context across HTTP/RPC/queue boundaries; sample aggressively because 100% traces at scale is usually unaffordable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions W3C/OTel propagation, span waterfalls for latency, and head/tail sampling with keep-errors/slow.

must_hit.point: Each unique metric label combo is a time series; high-cardinality labels like user_id cause metric explosion—identity belongs in logs/traces.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains Prometheus-style cardinality failure and where user identity should live instead.

must_hit.point: Page on user symptoms and error-budget burn rate, not every CPU blip; use grouping/inhibition and runbooks so pages mean act now.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates pages vs tickets/dashboards and cites burn-rate / symptom-based alerting.

probes: Define SLI, SLO, and SLA for a login API and what the error budget buys you.
Someone puts user_id on a Prometheus counter label—what breaks, and where should that identity live?

hints.1: Separate the measured thing, the internal target, and the customer contract.
hints.2: Budget = 1 − SLO; alerts should fire on user pain or budget burn; labels must stay low-cardinality.
hints.3: SLO tighter than SLA; 99.9% leaves 0.1% budget (~43 min/month); user_id on metrics explodes series—put it in logs/traces with trace_id.

phases.goal: Compare RED vs USE, black-box vs white-box, sampling cost, and Prometheus-fit vs billing-grade exactness.

must_hit.point: RED (Rate, Errors, Duration) for services/APIs; USE (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) for resources—use both layers in an incident.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Assigns RED to request path and USE to CPU/disk/NIC-style resources and says both are needed.

must_hit.point: Black-box probes like a user (uptime); white-box exposes internals (queue depth, saturation)—need both because white-box explains why and black-box catches external failures.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives an example like DNS fine but cert expired for black-box value.

must_hit.point: Prometheus fits ops metrics (pull, labels, PromQL, Alertmanager) but is not for exact billing or 'exactly once' accounting.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says reliable-enough ops data, not perfect accounting/billing.

probes: When would you use RED versus USE during an incident?
Why run both black-box probes and white-box saturation metrics?

hints.1: One checklist is about the service's requests; the other is about the machine/resource.
hints.2: RED = rate/errors/duration; USE = utilization/saturation/errors; black-box ≈ user probe, white-box ≈ internals.
hints.3: Use RED on APIs and USE on CPU/disk/NIC; black-box catches cert/DNS-class failures white-box may miss.

phases.goal: Close an HLD with golden signals/SLOs, walk an incident across pillars, and sketch a metrics platform with correlation.

must_hit.point: Closing a design: name golden signals, pick availability/latency SLIs, state one SLO sentence, and show where logs/metrics/traces attach on the diagram.
must_hit.evidence_hint: For Instagram/URL shortener/chat-style design, ties signals + SLI/SLO + three pillars into the whiteboard.

must_hit.point: Incident path for p99 checkout spike: metrics → traces (slow span) → logs via trace_id → fix; do not page on every non-user-facing blip.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates pillar-hopping investigation and what stays ticket/dashboard-only.

must_hit.point: Across async boundaries (e.g. OrderPlaced on a queue), propagate trace context; consumer lag is a metric, while the trace shows where latency was spent.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates lag/saturation metrics from span waterfall across producer/consumer.

must_hit.point: Design metrics platform (senior): agents → buffer → TSDB → query/alert; call out cardinality, retention/downsampling, and alert freshness vs dashboard eventual consistency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches Datadog-style path and names scale traps without claiming to invent a TSDB.

probes: You just designed a chat system—close it with golden signals, two SLIs, one SLO, and where each pillar plugs in.
p99 checkout latency spiked—walk the investigation, then sketch ingest→TSDB→alert for a metrics platform.

hints.1: End every HLD with how you know it's healthy: signals, an SLO sentence, and correlated telemetry.
hints.2: Investigation order is usually metrics → trace spans → logs by trace_id; platform sketch is agents, buffer, TSDB, dashboards/alerts.
hints.3: Availability + latency SLIs, p99 vs SLO, shared trace_id across pillars; for Datadog-style, mention cardinality, retention tiers, and freshness vs eventual dashboards.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Monitoring answers known threshold questions; observability uses correlated logs/metrics/traces to answer novel 'why this user/request' questions.
Averages hide the tail; interview default is track p50/p95/p99 and alert when p99 breaches the SLO.
RED for every service/API (rate, errors, duration); USE for every resource (utilization, saturation, errors); use both in an incident.
Black-box probes user-visible health; white-box exposes internals that explain why—you need both.

tradeoffs.topic: Symptom/budget-burn alerts vs raw CPU alerts
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Page on user symptoms and error-budget burn; CPU blips without user impact are tickets/dashboards, with grouping/inhibition/runbooks.

tradeoffs.topic: High-cardinality labels on metrics vs identity in logs/traces
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Unbounded labels (user_id, raw URL paths) explode time series; put high-cardinality identity in structured logs/traces linked by trace_id.
Full sampling at high QPS blows cost/collectors; sample (head or tail) and always retain errors/slow requests.
SLO is the tighter internal target; SLA is the looser contract—setting them equal means the first SLO miss is already a breach.

tradeoffs.topic: Prometheus for ops metrics vs exact billing
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prometheus is for reliable-enough operational metrics and alerting, not exact billing or exactly-once accounting.

tradeoffs.topic: Three disconnected tools vs correlated observability
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Separate log/metric/trace tools without shared IDs fail interviews; want one investigation path via trace_id/correlation (e.g. LGTM-style).

gotchas.trap: Quoting five nines without knowing ~5 min downtime/year, or confusing durability (S3 11 nines) with availability SLOs.
gotchas.correction: Know what each nines figure means in downtime, and keep durability promises separate from availability SLOs.

gotchas.trap: Alerting on CPU alone while user-facing error rate is fine, or ignoring saturation until OOM.
gotchas.correction: Alert on user symptoms and saturation trends that predict pain; CPU without user impact should not page.

gotchas.trap: Logging PII/secrets, or unstructured logs with no trace_id so pillars cannot be joined.
gotchas.correction: Use structured logs with safe fields plus request_id/trace_id; scrub secrets/PII.

gotchas.trap: Claiming exactly-once metrics or using Prometheus for billing.
gotchas.correction: Treat Prometheus as ops telemetry—reliable enough for alerts, not perfect accounting.

gotchas.trap: 100% trace sampling 'for correctness' at high QPS.
gotchas.correction: Sample aggressively; always keep errors and slow requests to preserve debuggability without melting collectors.

gotchas.trap: Setting SLA == SLO with zero buffer.
gotchas.correction: Keep SLO stricter than SLA so internal misses do not immediately become contract breaches.

gotchas.trap: Drawing three tools with no correlation story.
gotchas.correction: Show shared trace_id/request_id and one path: metrics → traces → logs.
